Inference Guide

This guide covers invoking deployed SageMaker endpoints for classification and segmentation predictions.

Prerequisites

  • A deployed endpoint in InService status (see Deployment Guide)

  • The endpoint’s task type: classification or segmentation

Invoking an Endpoint

Via the Dashboard UI

  1. Go to the Inference tab

  2. Select the endpoint from the dropdown

  3. Choose the input method:

    • S3 URI — enter the S3 path to your file

    • File Upload — upload a file directly from your browser

  4. Click Invoke

  5. View the response in the results panel

Via the API — S3 URI input

curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/inference/invoke \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "endpoint_name": "spine-classifier-v2",
    "task_type": "classification",
    "input_type": "s3_uri",
    "input_value": "s3://my-bucket/test/image.dcm"
  }'

Via the API — File upload (raw bytes)

curl -X POST "http://localhost:8000/api/inference/invoke-local?endpoint_name=spine-classifier-v2&task_type=classification" \
  --data-binary @/path/to/image.dcm

Optional: save result to S3

Add output_s3_uri to save the response:

curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/inference/invoke \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "endpoint_name": "spine-classifier-v2",
    "task_type": "classification",
    "input_type": "s3_uri",
    "input_value": "s3://my-bucket/test/image.dcm",
    "output_s3_uri": "s3://my-bucket/results/"
  }'

The result is saved to s3://<prefix>/<endpoint_name>-result.json.

Supported Input Formats

Classification endpoints

Format

How to send

DICOM (.dcm)

Raw bytes with Content-Type: application/dicom, or S3 URI, or base64

PNG / JPG

Same as DICOM — raw bytes, S3 URI, or base64

S3 URI

JSON: {"file_path": "s3://bucket/key.dcm"}

Local path

JSON: {"file_path": "/path/to/image.dcm"}

Base64

JSON: {"file_path": "<base64-encoded bytes>"}

Segmentation endpoints

Format

How to send

NIfTI (.nii.gz)

Raw bytes with Content-Type: application/octet-stream

S3 URI

JSON: {"s3_uri": "s3://bucket/subject/img.nii.gz"}

Local path

JSON: {"file_path": "/path/to/volume.nii.gz"}

Base64

JSON: {"file_path": "<base64-encoded NIfTI bytes>"}

Response Formats

Classification

{
  "predictions": [[0.1034, 0.1202, 0.1366, 0.0866, 0.1258, 0.1408, 0.1155, 0.1713]],
  "predicted_class": [7],
  "confidence": [0.1713]
}

Field

Type

Description

predictions

list[list[float]]

Probability array per input (batched)

predicted_class

list[int]

Index of the highest-probability class

confidence

list[float]

Probability of the predicted class

Segmentation

{
  "mask_nifti_b64": "<base64-encoded .nii.gz bytes>",
  "shape": [128, 128, 64],
  "voxels_positive": 14823,
  "voxels_total": 1048576,
  "volume_fraction": 0.0141
}

Field

Type

Description

mask_nifti_b64

string

Base64-encoded binary mask as a NIfTI file

shape

list[int]

Dimensions of the output mask

voxels_positive

int

Number of positive (foreground) voxels

voxels_total

int

Total voxels in the mask

volume_fraction

float

Ratio of positive voxels to total

To save the segmentation mask locally:

import base64

mask_bytes = base64.b64decode(response["mask_nifti_b64"])
with open("mask.nii.gz", "wb") as f:
    f.write(mask_bytes)

CLI Tools

For quick testing without the dashboard:

Classification

python tests/invoke_endpoint.py --s3-uri s3://bucket/image.dcm --endpoint my-endpoint
python tests/invoke_endpoint.py --image /path/to/image.dcm --endpoint my-endpoint

Segmentation

python test_endpoint_segmentation.py --endpoint my-seg-endpoint \
    --s3-uri s3://bucket/subject/img.nii.gz

python test_endpoint_segmentation.py --endpoint my-seg-endpoint \
    --local /path/to/volume.nii.gz

python test_endpoint_segmentation.py --endpoint my-seg-endpoint \
    --s3-uri s3://bucket/img.nii.gz --save-mask /tmp/mask.nii.gz

Troubleshooting

Issue

Cause

Fix

Empty mask (0 positive voxels)

Input outside expected HU range

Check that input is CT data in [-100, 500] HU range

ModelError

Inference script crash

Check CloudWatch logs for the endpoint

Timeout

Volume too large

Use async endpoint or a larger instance type

ValidationException

Endpoint not InService

Wait for deployment to complete or check for failures
